ACME Integrations (customer): Hey, we're seeing embeddings responses flip between 768 and 512 dims intermittently after upgrading the SDK. Also p90 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~2s for some requests. Request id 0a9f3c is one example.

Jen (support): Sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact payload, model, and whether this is hosted/dedicated/private?

ACME Integrations (customer): Hosted. model=redwood/embedding-large-v2, client lib 1.4.0 -> 1.5.0. Sample curl we used: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood/embedding-large-v2","input":["doc A","doc B"]}'`
Sometimes response vectors are length 512 with no error.

Jen (support): Can you share the last 5 request ids and timestamps? I've opened a ticket and tagging eng.

ACME Integrations (customer): Sure — ids: 0a9f3c, 0a9f4d, 0a9f5e, 0a9f6a, 0a9f88 (all in last 10m). We didn't change server-side config, only bumped client SDK.

Jen (support): Logged. Escalating to eng-runtime and ml: @Maya (eng-runtime) @Tariq (ml-onboarding) — can you take a look?

Maya (eng-runtime): Thanks. Quick question — did you or the SDK change max_batch_size or introduce any new batching flags?

ACME Integrations (customer): The SDK defaults changed in 1.5.0 to set desired_max_batch_size=64 (previously 16). We didn't explicitly set anything.

Liam (sre): I'm pulling logs for the time window. I see batches coalescing up to 64 and several warnings around batch key mismatch. Snippet from runtime logs:
```
2026-03-17T14:05:12.345Z batcher INFO slotting batch_id=bn-43 max_size=64 model_key=redwood/embedding-large-v2@v2
2026-03-17T14:05:12.349Z runtime WARN embedding_vector_len=512 expected=768 request_id=0a9f3c batch_id=bn-43
2026-03-17T14:05:12.350Z routing INFO fallback_to_variant=model-small-quantized reason=capacity
```
Maya (eng-runtime): That looks like routing fallback to a smaller variant under capacity pressure. But embedding-large-v2 should not produce 512. Two hypotheses: 1) batching logic is coalescing heterogeneous model variants into the same GPU batch (bad batch key equality), or 2) a model-variant produced 512 but was incorrectly tagged as the large model.

Tariq (ml-onboarding): Also possible: dynamic batching merged requests with different model_version metadata when slotting. If the SDK switched default batching config, the larger batch size increases chance of mixing queued requests from fallback route. Quick repro: send mixed requests with allow_fallback=true and desired_max_batch_size=64 and you'll see dimension mismatch.

Jen (support): ACME, can you reproduce if you pin the exact model version or reduce max_batch_size?

ACME Integrations (customer): Trying now — will report back.

Maya (eng-runtime): In the meantime I'll add a guard in batcher to validate per-request expected_dim before executing the kernel and reject the batch with a clear error instead of silently returning mixed dim vectors. That should be a short-term safety net. Long-term fix: stricter batch key (include model_variant+quantization flags). I'll open a PR.

Liam (sre): Workaround: set desired_max_batch_size=16 or set routing: strict (disable fallback). I also added an alert rule for `embedding_dim_mismatch_count > 0` and a dashboard tile.

ACME Integrations (customer): We pinned the model version and set desired_max_batch_size=16 — latency p90 back to ~150ms and dims are stable at 768. Thanks.

Jen (support): Created support ticket SUP-12345 and recommended the above workaround to the customer. Will monitor for the patch.

Maya (eng-runtime): Opened MR #456 with batch-key tightening + dimension validation tests. Starting canary in staging.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy started for eng-runtime at 1788882400 — rolling 10% -> 50% traffic.

Tariq (ml-onboarding): ETA for full patch rollout is ~4h after canary looks good. I'll add a unit test to catch mixed-model coalescing.

ACME Integrations (customer): Confirmed workaround is good for us, we'll wait for the patch. Thanks for the fast triage.

Jen (support): Great — marking this thread as triaged. I'll update SUP-12345 when MR is promoted and follow up with ACME. :thumbsup:

Maya (eng-runtime): After deploy I'll also add a metric for `batch_model_variant_entropy` to detect heterogeneous batches earlier.

Liam (sre): Closing loop on ops side once canary is green. Keeping the alert on.

ACME Integrations (customer): Appreciated — please share the release note when fixed.
